sections.title: Computer Misuse and digital seizure
sections.summary: Digital devices must be lawfully seized and forensically handled. Screenshots alone may not establish integrity without examiner evidence.
sections.keywords: device seizure, forensic, hash, cybercrime, screenshot

sections.title: Fair hearing
sections.summary: Accused persons are entitled to a fair hearing. Late disclosure or concealment of unused material may breach fair-trial obligations.
sections.keywords: disclosure, unused material, fair trial, abuse of process

sections.title: Prosecution disclosure
sections.summary: Prosecution must disclose material relevant to the defence. Schedules should be kept current; failure risks stay or abuse-of-process applications.
sections.keywords: disclosure schedule, MG6, unused material, withheld

sections.title: Data protection in investigations
sections.summary: Personal data in case files must be processed lawfully with access controls and retention limits appropriate to public-sector investigations.
sections.keywords: PII, personal data, retention, access log

sections.title: Corroboration and proof
sections.summary: Prosecution must prove the case beyond reasonable doubt. Uncorroborated single-witness cases require careful assessment of consistency and independent support.
sections.keywords: sole witness, uncorroborated, consistent, CCTV confirms

sections.title: Documentary evidence
sections.summary: Documents require proof of authenticity. Copies may need certification or a witness to prove the original or business-records foundation.
sections.keywords: original document, certified copy, business record, photocopy

sections.title: Electronic records
sections.summary: Electronic records must be authenticated. Hash values, forensic imaging, and examiner evidence support integrity arguments for digital exhibits.
sections.keywords: hash, forensic image, WhatsApp, digital, metadata

sections.title: Opinion and expert evidence
sections.summary: Expert opinion requires proof of qualifications, methodology, and reliable procedure. Informal opinions without report are vulnerable on cross-examination.
sections.keywords: expert report, forensic, laboratory, methodology, calibration

sections.title: Real evidence and identification
sections.summary: Physical exhibits must be identifiable and continuity must be provable. Identification evidence is scrutinised where witness observation conditions are poor.

sections.title: Hearsay rule and exceptions
sections.summary: Hearsay is generally excluded unless brought within a statutory or common-law exception. Prosecution should identify the exception and call the maker where required.

sections.title: Fairness when taking statements
sections.summary: Statements should be taken fairly with appropriate cautions and, where practicable, contemporaneous recording. Interpreter use must be documented.
sections.keywords: caution, recorded interview, interpreter, unsigned, verbal only

sections.title: Police powers and lawful process
sections.summary: TTPS powers must be exercised lawfully. Statements and seizures must follow established procedure and internal authorisation policies.
